We store both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses in a single data structure as defined. We suspect that ws_in4_addr/ws_in6_addr will not be able to replicate the exact condition.
please replace by tvb_get_ipv4/tvb_get_ipv6

tvb_get_ipv4 & tvb_get_ipv6 both give the result as guint32 value. While, what we want is to store the data in a ip_addr_t format which can be later used to display the IP addresses as a string. Further, the struct can be used to store both IPv4 & IPv6 addresses in a single object depending on the family.
there is already wireshark function to display ip to string...
Wireshark function to display ip to string cannot be used. We have a different format, ip_addr_t, which is read from packet.

Even after using next_tvb in the parent dissector (packet-aruba-papi.c), the tvb for UBT doesn't start in the intended offset. So, that's why the hardcoding of offset has been done.
Why? This should not be the case, please explain what's happening.

If we comment out the if condition and the hardcoding of the offset, the offset again starts at the start of the PAPI protocol. So, basically UBT protocol dissector tries to dissect the data under PAPI protocol too.
If the call to dissector_try_uint_new() is properly done with a new TVB containing the PAPI payload only, this should not be the case. Your comment suggest there is a bug in your code.

Hi @pquantin , 
Spacing in these fields is required in this format for ease of readability and to quickly understand and figure out what offset has which value. In the Active and Standby Map these values values will range from -1 till 11 and each one of these 256 value in active map can fall in these values. Same is for Standby Map (-1 till 11), while L2Connect has (0 and 1). All three have a relation with each other. In our internal consumption of data we have come up with this to be the best format for quick reading and understanding of the information and hence the spaces have been added intentionally for proper formatting.
It would be great if you could kindly allow this formatting with spaces so that these packet captures can help us and will match with our logs.

Please following the Wireshark, if you want to include this protocol

We would like to keep the display filter as just ubt. This is so that it is easier for the user to search for UBT packets. In reference to PAPI protocol dissector, it also uses just "papi" as the display filter. In the same fashion, we would like to keep ubt as the display filter string.

FT_IPv4 or FT_IPv6 ?

BASE_DEC for MTU ?
